title: Hardship and Protective Holds: Rolling Hold-Day Limits, Grant Limits and Waiting Periods
content:
Each tier of **Hardship and Protective Holds** carries its own limits on how much hold time one placed account may receive in any rolling 12 months, how many grants of the tier the account may receive in that period, and how long the account must wait between holds and after a denial. The figures below are per placed account and per tier.

## Definitions

- **Rolling 12-month hold-day maximum** — the largest number of hold days on one account in any rolling 12 months, counting holds of tiers whose days count toward the annual limit.
- **Counts toward the annual limit** — whether days of this tier count toward the rolling 12-month hold-day limit (yes or no).
- **Grants per account in 12 months** — holds of this tier one account may be granted in any rolling 12 months, a whole number.
- **Cooling-off days** — calendar days after the most recent hold on the account ended before a hold of this tier may start.
- **Reapply wait after denial** — calendar days after a denial of this tier before the consumer may request it again on the same account.

## Limits table

| Tier | Rolling 12-month hold-day maximum | Counts toward the annual limit | Grants per account in 12 months | Cooling-off days | Reapply wait after denial (days) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 30-Day Hardship Pause | 60 | Yes | 2 | 60 | 0 |
| Documented Hardship Hold | 120 | Yes | 1 | 90 | 30 |
| Disaster Relief Hold | 180 | No | 2 | 0 | 0 |
| Financial Assistance Review Hold | 240 | Yes | 1 | 0 | 0 |
| Long-Term Hardship Hold | 365 | Yes | 1 | 180 | 60 |
| Military Service Hold | 365 | No | 2 | 0 | 0 |

## Points of reading

- Days of a Disaster Relief Hold or a Military Service Hold do not count toward the rolling 12-month hold-day limit, because both tiers show "No" in the counting column.
- A tier with 0 cooling-off days has no cooling-off period after the most recent hold on the account ended; a tier with a reapply wait of 0 days has no waiting period after a denial.
- Only the Documented Hardship Hold (30 days) and the Long-Term Hardship Hold (60 days) carry a waiting period after a denial.

## Illustration (hypothetical)

An account has received one 30-Day Hardship Pause in the last rolling 12 months. The tier allows 2 grants per account in that period, so the count of grants (one) has not yet reached the tier's figure. Had the same account received a Documented Hardship Hold instead, the count of one grant would already equal that tier's figure of 1.
